headline: Napoli under pressure host Roma, the market's narrow favourites
summary: Napoli's director said Max Allegri is 'absolutely not in doubt' after the president asked to be reassured, following two straight defeats. Now Roma visit, 3rd in Serie A with 17 points. Gasperini's side won 4-0 at Slovan Bratislava on Tuesday without conceding, though Italian media report Paulo Dybala is out. Napoli's midweek win still cost them 2.69 expected goals, and Scott McTominay scored 2 on his return from a heart procedure. The market, margin removed, makes Roma narrow favourites at 37.8%, and the 2.5-goal line is a coin flip at 50.9% over. It sees a level night in Naples.
read: Napoli host Roma with Max Allegri's job being discussed in public after two straight defeats, while Roma arrive third in Serie A on the back of a 4-0 Champions League win. The market makes Roma narrow favourites at 37.8% to Napoli's 34.4%, with the handicap set level and the goal line sitting almost exactly at two and a half.

facts.fact: Napoli director Giovanni Manna said coach Max Allegri is 'absolutely not in doubt', after president Aurelio De Laurentiis asked to be 'reassured' following two straight defeats.
facts.meaning: Napoli go into a home game against the side third in Serie A with their coach's position being debated in public.

facts.fact: Roma are the market's narrow favourites in Naples at 37.8% to win, against Napoli's 34.4%.
Italian media report Roma are without Paulo Dybala, with Pellegrini's injury complicating Gasperini's attacking-midfield choices.
facts.meaning: Roma's creative options behind the strikers are thinner than usual for the trip to Naples.

facts.fact: Roma sit third in Serie A with 17 points from seven games.
facts.meaning: They arrive as the higher-placed of the two and the only one of them in the top four.

facts.fact: Roma beat Slovan Bratislava 4-0 on Tuesday with a 3.19 to 0.04 expected-goals advantage, a second straight win without conceding.
facts.meaning: Gasperini's side travel to Naples on their best run of the past month, and Gasperini rested Malen in midweek with this game in mind.

facts.fact: Napoli beat Bodo/Glimt 4-3 for their first Champions League win of the season but conceded 2.69 expected goals in doing it.
facts.meaning: The win ended the losing run, yet the game was open at the back — the defensive softness Allegri himself flagged afterwards.

facts.fact: The market has the 2.5-goal line as a coin flip: 50.9% over, with the fair total at 2.54 goals.
facts.meaning: Two or three goals is the expected night — the market does not see a rout in either direction.

facts.fact: Napoli lost 1-0 at Venezia on 17 October having created 2.36 expected goals.
facts.meaning: The result that fed the pressure on Allegri was not a bad performance — Napoli made the chances and did not take them.

sources.fact: Napoli director Giovanni Manna said coach Max Allegri 'is absolutely not in doubt' and that president Aurelio De Laurentiis wanted to be 'reassured' after two defeats, ahead of the Bodo/Glimt match.
Napoli beat Bodo/Glimt 4-3 in the Champions League, their first win of this season's competition.
Scott McTominay scored twice in the 4-3 win over Bodo/Glimt, his first goals since a procedure for a minor cardiac arrhythmia that kept him out for a month.
Allegri said after the 4-3 win that Napoli were 'too fragile' but that Kevin De Bruyne 'is going to really enjoy himself playing in front of the defence'.
Napoli lost 1-0 away to Venezia in Serie A, part of the run of two defeats that preceded the Bodo/Glimt win.
Sky pundit Ugolini wrote that, missed penalty aside, De Bruyne doesn't seem to have 'the attitude of someone who made the right choice in coming to Napoli'.
Roma beat Slovan Bratislava 4-0 at the Olimpico for their first Champions League victory of the season, with goals from Hermoso, Molina, Pisilli and Malen.

Italian media report that Roma are without Paulo Dybala and that Pellegrini's injury complicates Gasperini's attacking-midfield choices, while Bryan Cristante's return is a positive sign after his knee problem.
